The metal shaft, the most critical part of the part was poorly machined. The first crusher blade that I slid onto the shaft fit perfectly until it got about 3/8 inch from the end of the flat part of the shaft and wouldn't go any farther. So I had to dig out the Dremel tool then go buy a small grinding stone so I could re-machine the last 3/8 inch of the flat part of the shaft. This meant grinding a small amount on one side of the shaft and trying the blade. Then grinding the other side of the shaft and trying the blade. Doing this until the blade would slide all the way down the shaft but still be a snug fit so the center hole of the crusher blade didn't get distorted by a loose shaft in that area.
This turned a 30 minute repair job into over half a day.
How does BlueStar machine a shaft perfectly except for 3/8 inch from the end of the flattened sides of the shaft? That's just por quality control.
BlueStar needs to look into the manufacturing of this part. Evidently this is a recent issue because the only other review that mentions this problem was the one Angel did on Dec. 21, 2018. Broke the blades on mine when the ice maker quit and I started freezing ice cube tray ice and dumping it in the ice bin. Don't Do This! Ice tray, store ice is Larger than the cubes from the ice maker - they will jam and break the plastic screw blades. Finally did what I should have - took ice maker apart, fixed the ice rotator dispenser, replaced the auger, and, ice again.
CAVEAT: Pay VERY close attention to the ice chopping blades on the front of the auger you are replacing. Do Not remove them until You Are Sure you know the Exact order how to put them back on the new auger. THESE BLADES AND SPACERS GO ON IN A SPECIFIC ORDER AND THE BLADES IN A SPECIFIC ROTATION DIRECTION. I did not and spent a few wasted hours searching the internet before I got them back on the right way. And, be careful, there are small metal washesr between the spacers and are easy to drop and spend a long time finding them.
